description: Composite of two same-type work-hardening-index plots. Both panels plot ln(dσ/dε) (natural log of the strain-hardening rate, dimensionless) on the y axis, with labelled gridlines at 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11, against lnε (natural log of true strain) on the x axis, ticked from −5 to 0. (a) Steel M1: legend gives grey squares = M1-SS and black triangles = M1-30; solid straight segments are drawn through the scattered points. Grey labels mark "Stage I" (steep near-linear fall from between the 10 and 11 gridlines at lnε ≈ −5) and "Stage III" (slight rise then drop near the right end of the axis); black labels mark "Stage I" and "Stage II" (flat plateau between the 7 and 8 gridlines, below the grey curve). Two dotted vertical dividers sit near lnε ≈ −4.2 and −2.0. (b) Steel M2: magenta squares = M2-SS, red triangles = M2-30; both curves almost superimpose, each labelled Stage I (steep linear-fitted fall) and Stage II (plateau between the 7 and 8 gridlines, slightly higher than in (a)), separated by one dotted vertical line near lnε ≈ −3.7; no Stage III label appears. The figure shows that M1's unaged and aged conditions differ (different plateau level, extra third stage in M1-SS), whereas M2's two conditions coincide, i.e. Ti/V-modified precipitation barely alters work-hardening behaviour.

subfigures.description: Work-hardening-index plot for M1: y axis ln(dσ/dε) (ticks 7–11), x axis lnε (−5 to 0). Grey squares M1-SS and black triangles M1-30, with solid linear-fit lines through the steep branch. Grey text labels Stage I and Stage III (M1-SS), black text labels Stage I and Stage II (M1-30); two dotted vertical dividers near lnε ≈ −4.2 and −2.0. The aged M1-30 plateau lies below the M1-SS plateau.

Work-hardening-index plot for M2 with the same axes as (a). Magenta squares M2-SS and red triangles M2-30; the two datasets nearly overlap over the whole range. Magenta and red labels each mark Stage I (steep linear descent) and Stage II (plateau), separated by a single dotted vertical line near lnε ≈ −3.7; no Stage III is labelled.

observations.observation: Both panels plot ln(dσ/dε) versus lnε with no units, y-axis tick labels 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and x-axis from −5 to 0.
Panel (a) legend identifies grey squares as M1-SS and black triangles as M1-30.

In panel (a) the grey M1-SS data are annotated with 'Stage I' and 'Stage III', while the black M1-30 data are annotated with 'Stage I' and 'Stage II', i.e. the labels are colour-coded to the two conditions.
Panel (a) contains two dotted vertical dividers, one near lnε ≈ −4.2 (start of short plateau before the long flat region) and one near lnε ≈ −2.0 (onset of the third stage).

The M1-30 plateau in (a) lies between the 7 and 8 gridlines and sits clearly below the M1-SS plateau, which stays nearer the 7.5 level; M1-SS then rises slightly and drops at the right end of the axis (Stage III).
Panel (b) legend identifies magenta squares as M2-SS and red triangles as M2-30.
In panel (b) the M2-SS and M2-30 curves almost coincide throughout Stage I and Stage II, with a single dotted vertical divider near lnε ≈ −3.7 and no Stage III label.
The caption states that the solid lines in these plots are linear fits of the plotted points.
No numeric data values are printed on either panel; only the axis tick labels are available as quantitative anchors.
The citing text states that the work hardening of solid-solution samples without Ti and V is divided into three stages, whereas after aging it is divided into two stages.

The citing text states that, compared with M1, the work-hardening-index curves of M2 before and after aging almost coincide, indicating that uniform κ-carbide precipitation affects the work-hardening ability of the low-density steel.

The citing text states that the first stage is a rapid dislocation-slip stage causing a rapid decrease in the work-hardening index, and that in the second stage plane slip of dislocations is the main deformation mode.
